findings.passage: At a few points the easier or more rewarding option was open and he reports taking the other, for a reason he states as right or owed.
findings.problem: The edit replaced the type argument after the frozen review. The draft's discriminator (limits chosen and kept, pain reframed in order to stay, a judge located inside) was withdrawn; this narrower one was written in its place; Type 3 was promoted to a co-alternative in the answer, the FAQ and the description; and confidence went from medium to low. None of the six reviewers saw any of it. The standard requires a hold for --refresh --expanded-review when editing changes the type thesis after the frozen review, and the enneagram reviewer said the same of promoting Type 3.
findings.acceptance_test: The run is repeated with --refresh --expanded-review so all six roles review the rebuilt argument, the Type 3 comparison and the new title against a frozen copy. No release is built from this run's reviews.

findings.passage: That is this profile's inference from four moments in twelve years, and the reasons are all his own telling. It is enough to put Type 1 first. It is not enough to settle the question.
findings.problem: The article is right about itself, and under the standard that means it cannot release as a standard profile. No discriminator survives: the candidate rests on four self-reported moments, each with a rival reading the article gives, two of them from the 2026 press window; the article says the Seven reading explains more of what he says drives him and that it found no clean test against Type 3. The evidence record agrees (confidence low, status insufficient_evidence). The open-case format does not apply to someone with fourteen years of public record.
findings.acceptance_test: Either research produces a defensible discriminator at medium confidence or better (named on-record testimony about how he responds when work falls short, or a documented choice where doing it his way cost him reception) and the evidence status returns to ready, or the page stays held or is folded into the Markiplier refresh with whatever type that evidence supports.

findings.problem: The edit cut this quotation in the way the jury faulted six others. The sentence in S11 (15:28-15:39) is 'I have to bend the rules as as much as necessary to be able to tell the story as well as I can, but I cannot break the rules', said about adapting one game, and the frozen draft quoted it whole. The candidate keeps only the absolute half, then builds the title, the meta_title ('The Rules He Says He Cannot Break') and the thesis question ('rules he says he cannot break') on it as a general statement about him. He said it of the game's rules, with a qualifier, and said nothing like it about the channel deletion.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence is quoted whole or the 'bend the rules as much as necessary' half is reported beside it, and the article says he was speaking about the game's rules. The title, meta_title and thesis question either name that one rule or stop attributing a general claim to him. C54 records the full sentence.

findings.passage: he drove home, told Nelson, "I think it's done," and then: "I break down for 30 minutes straight. I cried. Just curled up in a ball and cried. Not out of sadness."
findings.problem: This anecdote and its two direct quotations have no claim in the evidence inventory, and no claim cites S14, the video it comes from. The standard requires every direct quotation and thesis-supporting anecdote to be inventoried. The words themselves check out (S14 captions 04:16-04:50), and he dates the night 'a week before or maybe 2 weeks before' the January 30 release. Two smaller gaps: 'was like the fifth thing that I tried to do' appears in C84's claim text but not its passage, and the sentence 'one channel, one partner and the same friends for more than a decade', used against the Seven reading, has no passage of its own.
findings.acceptance_test: The inventory has a self_report claim citing S14 whose passage contains both quotations, with its limits (retold four months later, after the film succeeded; Nelson's account not on record). C84's passage includes the 'fifth thing' quotation, and the 'one channel, one partner' sentence is covered by a claim or reworded to what C38 and C83 support.

findings.passage: a former head moderator complained that he had not reached out, and he replied that he had seen no attempt to contact him, only an inactive marker beside their names.
findings.problem: Two small things in the one adverse episode. The report says his statement came in replies to other users who criticized him, one of whom called him 'hubristic'; 'he replied' reads as a reply to the head moderator. And the reader's link is an unpinned Wayback URL (web/2025/...) that on 2026-10-11 resolved to capture 20260125045054, which returned HTTP 500 twice.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence says he made the statement in replies to other users, per the same report. The link and the frontmatter citation point to a specific working capture, for example 20250803103929 or 20260205010007.

findings.passage: On a live panel of creators hosted by Colin and Samir in June 2026
findings.problem: Upload dates are given as the dates things were said, and one is wrong. The video's intro says the conversation took place at Press Publish LA on the Fox lot; the organizers' page dates that event May 28, 2026, and in the conversation the film is still 'coming out on YouTube' (it did on May 31). June 11, 2026 is when the video was posted. The article says 'in June 2026' twice. 'On May 20, 2022, Anthony Padilla ... asked' has the same form: that is the upload date, and the recording date is not in the record.
findings.acceptance_test: The panel is dated May 28, 2026 with the video's June 11 publication date kept in the citation, in both places and in C26 and C69. The Padilla sentence says the interview was published on May 20, 2022.

findings.passage: In 2017 he had offers in hand and turned them down as unearned. In 2022 he called his income unfair and said his answer was to give it away.
findings.problem: Two of the four moments are stated more firmly than the sources. The 2017 offers are known only from his own sentence, his first reason there is 'I didn't come for that', and the evidence record notes that no offer is documented. In 2022 he says 'I donate to charity'; 'so you give a lot of it away' is Padilla's line, and he adds that he has a nice house and car and will be comfortable for life. The FAQ goes further and says he 'says he wanted the open option' in all three examples; he says that only about the film.
findings.acceptance_test: The paragraph says he said he was turning offers down and gives his own words for what he does with the money. The FAQ answer attributes the stated wish only to the film, or is reworded to match the body ('the easier or more rewarding option was open').

findings.passage: Against them stand the fear he calls his biggest, which is lost novelty
findings.problem: The gloss is narrower than the source and tilts the night toward Type 7. In S05 (06:22-07:15) 'that feeling' is 'knowing that what you say influences people', that 'each and every one of those people matter', 'raw creation' and 'raw unexplored territory', and he restates the fear as 'losing my way on YouTube'. Connection to the audience is half of it, which bears on the Type 2 and Type 6 thread the article raises later.
findings.acceptance_test: The fear is described in his terms (the feeling of the early channel, including its closeness to viewers, and 'losing my way on YouTube'), or the sentence says novelty is one part of what he names.

findings.passage: Where the judge sits cannot carry the type. What the judge measures might.
findings.problem: The body is 4,328 words, 772 more than the frozen draft and well above the standard's 2,000-3,500 target, and three acceptance tests asked for no net growth. The last three sections run about 1,480 words of analysis, and the caution that the evidence is his own account is restated in at least six places.
findings.acceptance_test: The body is under about 3,900 words with no sourced context removed, mainly by stating the self-report caution once per section at most and tightening 'Where the judge sits' and 'What the record cannot show'.

research_tasks: Decision for DJ before anything else: rerun this subject as `Markiplier --refresh --expanded-review` on the live URL, or confirm a separate legal-name page with a plan that keeps the two pages from stating different types. The live page is Type 7.

Testimony: open the February 2026 Distractible episodes with Wade Barnes and Bob Muyskens about the film, and look for on-record accounts from Amy Nelson, Tyler Scheid, Seán McLoughlin, Philip Roy, Caroline Rose Kaplan, the makeup head named Anna on Lemonade Stand, and Lixian and Sam, whom he names in S14 as helping finish the film. Record whether they describe him redoing work that misses a standard, moving on to the next idea, or managing how it looks.

Type 1 against Type 3: find a dated choice where doing it the way he thought right cost him reception or standing. Read the Empire and Guardian two-star reviews to see whether they fault the slow opening he says a studio would have fixed, and read S11 25:00-1:05:00 and the rest of S13 for notes he refused before release.

Type 1 against Type 7: read the unread parts of S11, S13 and S32 and obtain the IndieWire interview (S30) for any account of what he does when a rule he set and his own wish diverge, beyond the single 'that's not the game' statement.

Audio check before release. YouTube refused caption and audio downloads from this machine on 2026-10-11, so I could run a second transcription only on recordings the draft stage had saved. Confirmed that way: every quotation from S08, S09, S10 and S15, and S05 up to 06:15. Still resting on machine captions alone: all quotations from S04, S11, S01, S02, S03, S06, S07, S21 and S22, and from S05 'my biggest fear', 'disappointing you guys', 'right steps', 'happier than I've ever been' and 'not quitting'. S08 also needs a listen for speaker attribution.
Moderator dispute: open the r/Markiplier posts and his replies (S31) and one more report; establish to whom he was replying and how much of his post was a joke.

Dates: settle his age at his father's death from a primary record (he says 18; July 4, 2008 is six days after a nineteenth birthday on a June 28, 1989 birth date). Correct the panel date to May 28, 2026.

Changing facts before any release: the final theatrical total from Box Office Mojo or The Numbers; whether a next feature has been announced since June 29, 2026 (a standard search on 2026-10-11 found none named, which is not conclusive); subscriber count; the Rotten Tomatoes score; whether the Nestor clip is still retrievable (it was on 2026-10-11).
After the above, rerun with --refresh --expanded-review so the six roles see the rebuilt argument.
